newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Seventeen hurt in Arab-Israeli Hebron clashes.
newsitem.headline: Seventeen hurt in Arab-Israeli Hebron clashes.

text.p: Fifteen Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers were wounded on Sunday in clashes between troops and stone-throwing Arab demonstrators in the West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses and hospital officials said.

The clashes broke out for the second straight day on the border between Palestinian-controlled parts of Hebron and Israeli-guarded Jewish enclaves in the centre of the city, home to 400 Jewish settlers.
Witnesses said 150 protesters throwing stones and firebombs clashed with Israeli troops in the narrow streets of Hebron -- home to around 100,000 Palestinians -- for nearly five hours.
In Jerusalem, masked supporters of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Fatah faction burned Israeli and U.S. flags.
The unrest underscored the fragility of Israel-PLO peace moves, deadlocked since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem three months ago.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the unrest had a political motive. He said it would not succeed.

"I think these things are not by chance and I do not think that they are spontaneous. I think that there is an organising hand and there is a political intent behind it...and it will not work," Netanyahu told reporters in Jerusalem.

Arafat told reporters after meeting co-Nobel peace laureate and former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres in Ramallah: "There's a deep crisis in the peace process caused by the Israeli government's refusal to implement the (peace) agreement."

Israel released a list of what it said were violations of the peace deal in Hebron by Arafat's Palestinian Authority ranging from exceeding the number and type of weapons allowed its forces to its entry into Israeli-ruled areas.
In Hebron, Israeli soldiers firing rubber bullets wounded 15 protesters, officials at Hebron's Alia Hospital said.

The radio said an Israeli border police officer was slightly wounded when a demonstrator armed with a slingshot hit him in the eye with a marble. The Israeli army said a second soldier was wounded in the unrest.
The army said joint Palestinian-Israeli patrols had stopped patrolling Palestinian-run parts of Hebron.
Witnesses said Palestinian police did not intervene to disperse demonstrators.
They said Israel had substantially beefed up its forces near the heavily fortified Jewish enclaves following more serious clashes on Saturday when 30 Palestinians were wounded.
Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January under an interim peace deal but kept troops to protect the settler enclaves in the town.
Palestinians are angry at a recent non-binding U.S. House of Representatives vote calling on President Bill Clinton to affirm Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state, say Jewish settlement building in Jerusalem pre-empts final peace talks on the city's fate.
Israel vows never to cede any part of the city. It captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and, in a move unrecognised by the international community, annexed it.
Peres, ousted by Netanyahu last year, said after meeting Arafat that the peace process was "deeply in trouble, but it is very far from being over. It will be continued in spite of everything."
